messages:
carla: FYI brought up kestrel-v2 ensemble (fp16 primary + int4 mirror) on dedicated canary. seeing weird duped tool invocations when parsing fails + retry kicks in. baseline fp16-only had 0.4% funcall parse fails; ensemble canary shows 1.9% parse fails + ~0.6% duplicated downstream calls.
carla: pattern: model emits a funcall, postprocess fails to parse (partial escape sequence), client retries, but mirror replica already succeeded and forwarded the tool call. dedupe at router misses because X-funcall-id header is only added at retry time.
devin: so the duplicate happens when primary fails parse and retry produces a different idempotency header than the mirror which succeeded earlier?
carla: exactly. replica responds faster for some samples (mirror reached token end earlier due to different chunk flush). primary later retries with new header -> tool-router treats it as new call.
sam: rough trace: 
```
[primary] emit: {"action":"send_email","args":{"to":"ops@...","body":"Hi\\nPlease..."}}  <-- parsing error due to broken escape 
[router] forwarded to mailbox v2 (mirror already forwarded earlier)
[primary retry id=retry-891] emit: {"action":"send_email",...} header X-funcall-id: retry-891
[router] forwarded again -> duplicate email
```
carla: tried increasing retry budget and repair heuristics, but duplicates persisted because dedupe key wasn't stable.
devin: quick mitigation: generate and attach a stable client-side funcall UUID at initial request time and pass that through both original and retry attempts (runtime should propagate header to mirror too). we should ensure SDK+runtime both set X-client-funcall-id before any emit.
sam: agree. additional safety: router-level short-window dedupe by (client-funcall-id, action_hash) for the canary traffic. if header missing, fallback to attempt-based dedupe with a TTL.
infra-bot: Canary report: kestrel-v2-ensemble total=12000, parse_fail=1.9%, duplicates_detected=0.58%
qa-bot: noted failure modes include escaped backslash sequences near end-of-output and multiline bodies. reproducer set attached in ticket.
sam: root cause hypotheses: (1) different chunk-flush heuristics between quantized mirror kernels and fp16 primary causing mirror to finish earlier, (2) JSON repair heuristics mutate identity of payload (e.g., normalize whitespace) so router dedupe hash mismatches, (3) SDK added header only on retry path.
devin: action plan: 1) immediate: SDK change to set stable X-client-funcall-id on request creation across all replicas and retries (canary-only flag), 2) router: implement weak dedupe window (5s) by client-funcall-id+action-type, 3) infra: capture token-flush timing histograms for primary vs mirror for failing samples and attach to kernel owners, 4) qa: run 50k replay with stable header to confirm dupes drop.
carla: patched SDK locally: stable-header param set and canary run with 5k samples shows duplicates drop to ~0.02% (close to noise). parse_fail still ~1.8% so we keep repair heuristics but duplicates addressed.
sam: long-term: prefer making postprocess idempotent (e.g., hold-off retries until mirror completion or use consensus ack) but that is heavier. put on roadmap after kernel flush data.
devin: i'll open infra ticket and cc kernel owners. QA, kick off the 50k replay when infra toggles header propagation.
carla: thanks. i'll update the canary playbook with the SDK flag and add a dashboard tile for duplicate-toolcall-rate. tagging @sam @devin. :thumbsup:
